Hi Adam / Priya -

Thanks again for the time today - great conversation and super helpful to see the example flows you care about. Quick recap + proposed next steps:

What we heard:
- Primary use case: real-time assistant inside FinCo customer portal for policy & claims triage. Low latency is critical for live agent handoffs.
- Target latency: 95th percentile <= 150ms for short prompts (~1-2k input tokens), with burst tolerance up to 250ms.
- Throughput/concurrency: steady-state ~200 QPS across endpoints, with expected concurrency per model ~40-60 during peak.
- Context window: some workflows require long context (up to 32k tokens) for full-policy history; many calls will be 4-8k tokens.
- Streaming: preferred for agent UX (token-by-token), but final outputs also stored in transcripts.

What Redwood proposes next:
1) Technical sync between FinCo SRE + Redwood solutions (Rishi) to validate infra & concurrency plan (30-45m).
2) Provide a latency estimate matrix for your two primary model profiles (short: 1-2k input, long: 8-32k input) and streaming vs non-streaming. Rishi will attach estimates.
3) Trial configuration: set up a dedicated sandbox with 32k context-enabled model, QoS routing, and prefix caching.

Attachments: I attached the meeting notes and the initial latency estimate workbook from our side (redwood-latency-estimate-finco.xlsx).

Would you be available for a technical sync on Wed 24th at 10am PT? If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and include our SRE/solutions leads.

Thanks - looking forward to next steps.

Thanks Adam - noted.

Quick answers so Rishi can expand in the workbook:
- 95p <=150ms number is for warm inference with prefix/KV cache enabled and the model pinned to dedicated capacity (our Dedicated pool numbers). Cold (first request to a cold instance) can add ~50-150ms depending on model size and GPU warm-up; we mitigate with pre-warming for critical endpoints.
- For long context (8-32k): expect additional per-token processing overhead. Ballpark: 8k context (vs 1k) adds ~30-80ms p95 for final token in a typical autoregressive flow; 32k contexts can add 200-600ms p95 depending on kernel/attention mode and whether attention is chunked/flash-attn. Rishi will include a table.
- Streaming: streaming sessions maintain a small per-connection overhead; concurrency limits apply primarily to token throughput (QPS). We can support streaming at scale but will recommend separate routing (streaming pool) to keep non-streaming latency stable.

I'll send the invite for Wed 24th 10am PT and Rishi will attach the updated workbook before the call.

Best,
Marissa

Adam / Priya / Marissa -

Attaching the latency estimate workbook (redwood-latency-estimate-finco.xlsx). Notes / highlights from the workbook (high-level):

- Experimental setup: Dedicated GPU pool, model variant A (16B, quantized), batching tuned for low-latency (max batch size 8), KV prefix cache enabled for repeated context.

- Short prompt profile (1-2k tokens input, 50-200 tokens output):
  - Warm p50/p95 (non-streaming): ~45ms / ~120-150ms (final token)
  - Warm streaming p50/p95 (first tokens streaming): ~40ms / ~130-160ms (streaming introduces ~10-20ms per-token emit overhead)
  - Cold invocation delta: +80-150ms (model activation + cache warm-up)

- Medium context (4-8k tokens):
  - Non-streaming p95 delta vs short: +30-120ms depending on attention kernel and whether KV cache covers most context
  - Streaming: increased end-to-end latency for final token by similar delta; however user-perceived latency for early tokens remains close to short-prompt numbers if we stream initial tokens immediately.

- Long context (16-32k tokens):
  - Significant overhead due to attention memory & chunked attention processing. Ballpark p95: +150-600ms vs short prompts (larger range for 32k).
  - We recommend a hybrid approach: chunk the policy history into compressed embeddings for retrieval + shorter active window for generation to keep tail latency down.

- Concurrency / throughput:
  - Single GPU config (quantized 16B) tuned for low-latency: ~150-250 token/s output throughput per instance depending on sequence lengths.
  - To reach 200 QPS with 50-100 token outputs: scale to multiple instances + autoscaling buffer. We can provide exact capacity planning given your token mix.

- Streaming vs non-streaming routing:
  - Best practice: separate streaming pool with slightly higher headroom to avoid token-emit stalls impacting non-streaming SLOs.

Action items for Wed sync:
- Walk through the workbook numbers (I'll share screens) and validate FinCo token-mix assumptions.
- Validate pre-warm / warm-routes strategy for low-latency critical endpoints.
- Plan a 2-week sandbox (dedicated pool + telemetry) to measure real traffic and tune autoscaling/batching.

Attachment: redwood-latency-estimate-finco.xlsx (workbook with tables + assumptions)
